phases.message: The quarter closed on 30 September and I need to draw on our federal award and file the SF-425. Start here in Grantflow: read the rules, what we've already drawn, and the reports we've filed.
Now Docshelf. Read the award's terms and anything else in the folder that bears on what we can charge.
This is Ledgerline. Go through every entry coded to a federal award and note what each one is, when it was paid, and anything odd.
And Payroll Harbor: the quarter's pay for everyone charged to the award, against their timesheets.
Back in Grantflow. Add every cost the award should reimburse to the request, at the right amount, and file the SF-425 for the quarter. Then tell me what you left out and why.

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Award FA-2025-0417, period of performance 1 October 2025 to 30 September 2027. The quarter ended 30 September 2026; its SF-425 is due 30 October 2026. Topics: payment, allowable, personnel, report.

This award pays by reimbursement only (a specific condition under 2 CFR 200.208), so draw only for costs already paid. Add each cost to the request once: a cost already drawn cannot be drawn again. Charge only this award's own costs, incurred within the period of performance; costs from before it need the agency's written approval (2 CFR 200.458), and none has been given.

Unallowable under 2 CFR 200 Subpart E, whatever the fund code says: alcoholic beverages (200.423); entertainment, including social events and celebrations (200.438); fundraising and its events (200.442); lobbying and advocacy to a legislature (200.450); fines and penalties (200.441). A cost belonging to another award may not be shifted to this one (200.405(c)).

Salary and fringe are charged by what the certified timesheets record, not by a budget estimate or a payroll allocation (2 CFR 200.430(i)). Someone who spent 30% of their hours on this award's program is charged at 30% of the quarter's salary and fringe.

SF-425, cash basis, cumulative from the start of the award to the period end. 10a: reimbursements received. 10b: cash disbursed for the award. 10e: the federal share of expenditures, that is every allowable cost of this award paid by the period end, drawn or not. 10f: obligations incurred and not yet paid. No cost share on this award. Due 30 days after the quarter ends (2 CFR 200.328).
